Quick triage notes (what I ran so far):
- Observed a correlated increase in tail latency for AstraX3b across two host pools in us-west-2 (host-pool-7 + host-pool-9) starting 07:56 PDT.
- Error class: transient 502s (upstream timeout at GPU runtime) and soft timeouts from our load balancer when KV cache miss + long decode happened.
- No recent model checkpoint or config pushed within the last 12 hours.
- Autoscaler did not react fast enough due to an anomalous sequence-length distribution spike from a small set of customers (including Brightline) — long contexts causing GPU kernels to run slower than expected and hitting runtime timeouts.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:00 PDT):
1) Increased the concurrency cap for AstraX3b host-pools and temporarily raised the soft-timeout window to 6s for affected routes.
2) Enabled routing override for Brightline to AstraX3b-v2 (slightly different quantization and warmer KV cache) — currently 100% of Brightline traffic is on v2.
3) Began preheating extra instances and warming KV caches for high-seq customers.

Status: error rate for Brightline requests dropped from ~10% to ~0.8% in the last 12 minutes after routing change. We'll monitor for an hour then revert to normal routing if stable.

Attachments: logs_20260620.tar.gz (from Brightline) — I pulled runtime traces and included a small trace file in the shared drive.

I'll prepare a short postmortem draft after we stabilize.

Markus
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Subject: AstraX3b incident update and post-incident plan (Brightline)

Hi Lena —

Thank you again for the quick report and for the logs you attached; they helped us narrow the root cause. Below is a short summary and next steps.

What happened
- Between ~07:56–09:12 PDT on 2026-06-20 AstraX3b experienced elevated 502s and timeouts for a subset of customers with unusually long context lengths. The runtime's tail latency increased and, together with load-balancer soft-timeouts, produced the 502s you observed.

What we did for Brightline (customer-facing fixes)
- Immediately routed Brightline traffic to AstraX3b-v2 (warm KV cache + slightly different quant profile).
- Raised per-route soft-timeout threshold and pre-warmed additional instances to reduce queuing and decode latency.
- Monitored and confirmed error rate dropped from ~10% to <1% within 15 minutes.

Root cause (engineering summary)
- A surge in long-sequence requests from a small customer cohort caused a workload shift that exposed a tail-latency regression in AstraX3b's runtime path when combined with cold KV caches. The autoscaler and routing policy were not aggressive enough to avoid transient overload in two host pools.

Customer impact
- Brightline saw ~10% failed calls in the impacted window. No data loss or content leakage.

Next steps / remediation plan
- Short term: We will keep Brightline on AstraX3b-v2 for 24 hours while we observe.
- Medium term: Runtime team will ship a fix to reduce tail latency on long-context decodes and improve autoscaler sensitivity for mixed-length workloads (ETA: 7 days).
- We'll provide a final postmortem and a follow-up patch note once the runtime fix is validated.

Compensation / credits
- I opened a request for a service credit for the impacted window under BR-4392. I'll follow up with the paperwork and the exact credit calculation within 3 business days.
